or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

pier — script catalog and runner

pier provides a simple way to catalog, manage, and run short shell scripts and one-liners. It lets you add, remove, list, and execute scripts by alias, and stores human-readable metadata for easy discovery and reuse.

Basic features
- Add scripts with an alias and metadata
- List available scripts and their commands
- Run scripts by alias
- Edit or remove entries

Installation
- Download a prebuilt release for your platform from the project's releases page.
- Alternatively, install using your system or language package manager if a packaged build is provided.

Usage (summary)
- pier --help  # show help and available commands
- pier add <alias> --command "<shell command>"  # add a new script
- pier list  # list scripts
- pier run <alias>  # run a script
- pier remove <alias>  # remove a script

Configuration
pier uses a simple human-readable configuration (e.g. TOML) to store scripts and metadata. Example entry:

[scripts.example]
command = "echo Hello, world!"

Examples
- Add and run a sample script:
  pier add hello --command "echo Hello"
  pier run hello

For more usage examples and behavior, consult the project's documentation or the installed binary's help output (pier --help).

import subprocess, shutil, os
def setup(base):
    shutil.rmtree(base, ignore_errors=True)
    for d in ["cwd","xdg/pier","home/.config"]:
        os.makedirs(base+"/"+d, exist_ok=True)
    return base
def go(base, envextra, cwdfiles=(), xdgfiles=(), homefiles=(), note=""):
    setup(base)
    for f in cwdfiles:
        open(base+"/cwd/"+f,'w').write("[scripts.cwd_%s]\ncommand = 'echo %s'\n" % (f.replace('.','_'), f))
    for f in xdgfiles:
        open(base+"/xdg/pier/"+f,'w').write("[scripts.xdg_%s]\ncommand = 'echo %s'\n" % (f.replace('.','_'), f.replace('.','_')))
    for f in homefiles:
        open(base+"/home/"+f,'w').write("[scripts.home_%s]\ncommand = 'echo %s'\n" % (f.replace('.','_'), f.replace('.','_')))

    env["HOME"]=base+"/home"
    env.update(envextra)
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","list","-q"],cwd=base+"/cwd",capture_output=True,text=True,env=env)
    print("%-42s rc=%d out=%r err=%r" % (note or str(envextra), r.returncode, r.stdout.strip(), r.stderr.strip()))

    let mut prev_single = false;
    for (si, (title, args)) in sections.iter().enumerate() {
        lines.push(String::new());
        if si > 0 && prev_single {
            lines.push(String::new());
        }
        lines.push(format!("{}:", title));
        let longest = args.iter().map(|a| dw(&arg_display(a))).max().unwrap_or(2).max(2);
        let longest_usage = args.iter().map(|a| dw(&arg_usage(a))).max().unwrap_or(2).max(2);
        let spcs = longest_usage + 12;
        let col = 4 + longest + 4;
        let mut last_entry_single = false;
        for (ai, arg) in args.iter().enumerate() {
            if ai > 0 {
                lines.push(String::new());
            }
            let disp_s = arg_display(arg);
            let aline = format!("    {}    ", crate::table::pad_to(&disp_s, longest));
            let help_text = arg_help(arg, ctx, long);
            last_entry_single = !help_text.contains('\n');
            if nlh_mode {
                lines.push(aline);
                let wrapped: Vec<String> =
                    if spcs + max_line_len(&help_text) > term_w {
                        help_text
                            .split('\n')
                            .flat_map(|l| wrap_line(l, term_w - spcs))
                            .collect()
                    } else {
                        help_text.split('\n').map(|s| s.to_string()).collect()
                    };
                for wl in wrapped {
                    lines.push(format!("            {}", wl));
                }
            } else {
                let wrapped: Vec<String> = if spcs + max_line_len(&help_text) > term_w {
                    wrap_line(&help_text, term_w - spcs)
                } else {
                    vec![help_text.clone()]
                };
                let mut first = true;
                for wl in wrapped {
                    if first {
                        let mut l = aline.clone();
                        l.push_str(&wl);
                        lines.push(l);
                        first = false;
                    } else {
                        lines.push(format!("{}{}", " ".repeat(col), wl));
                    }
                }

import subprocess, os, shutil, unicodedata
base="/tmp/uw5"; shutil.rmtree(base,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(base)
cfg=base+"/c.toml"
def width_of(ch):
    if os.path.exists(cfg): os.remove(cfg)
    subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","-c",cfg,"config-init"],capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","-c",cfg,"add","-a","t","-d",ch*30,"--","c"],capture_output=True,text=True)

    cells=r.stdout.split("\n")[1].split("\u22ee")

    try:
        w=width_of(ch)
    except Exception as e:
        continue
    (zero if w<=27 else one).append(cp)
def ranges(lst):
    out=[]; 
    for c in lst:
        if out and out[-1][1]==c-1: out[-1][1]=c
        else: out.append([c,c])
    return out
print("Cf ZERO:", ["%04X-%04X"%(a,b) for a,b in ranges(zero)])
print("Cf ONE :", ["%04X-%04X"%(a,b) for a,b in ranges(one)])

import subprocess, os, shutil, unicodedata, random
base="/tmp/uwB"; shutil.rmtree(base,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(base)
cfg=base+"/c.toml"
def reset():
    if os.path.exists(cfg): os.remove(cfg)
    subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","-c",cfg,"config-init"],capture_output=True)
def w1(cp):
    reset()
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","-c",cfg,"add","-a","t","-d",chr(cp)*30,"--","c"],capture_output=True,text=True)
    if r.returncode!=0: return None
    rr=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","-c",cfg,"list"],capture_output=True,text=True)
    cells=rr.stdout.split("\n")[1].split("\u22ee")
    return len(cells[4])-2
def expected(cp):
    cat=unicodedata.category(chr(cp))
    ea=unicodedata.east_asian_width(chr(cp))
    if cat in ('Mn','Me'): return 0
    if ea in ('W','F') and cat not in ('Cn',): return 2
    return 1
random.seed(11)
pool=[cp for cp in range(0x20,0x110000) if unicodedata.category(chr(cp))[0]!='C']
s=random.sample(pool, 250)
bad=[]
for cp in s:
    w=w1(cp)
    e=expected(cp)
    # scale: observed = 30*w if w>0 else 27
    got = 0 if w==27 else w/30
    if got!=e: bad.append((hex(cp),got,e,unicodedata.category(chr(cp)),unicodedata.east_asian_width(chr(cp))))
print("mismatches:", len(bad))
for b in bad[:25]: print(b)
PY

    notwide.add(c)
wide=[cp for cp in wide if cp not in notwide]
def ranges(cps):
    out=[]
    for c in sorted(set(cps)):
        if out and out[-1][1]==c-1: out[-1][1]=c

    if row: lines.append("    " + ", ".join(row) + ",")
    lines.append("];")
    return "\n".join(lines)

fn parse_array(p: &mut Parser) -> Result<Value, ParseError> {
    let mut out: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
    let mut kind: Option<String> = None;
    loop {
        skip_ws_comments_newlines(p)?;
        match p.peek()? {
            Some((Token::RightBracket, _, _)) => {
                p.next()?;
                break;
            }
            None => return Err(eof_err(p)),
            _ => {}
        }
        let vstart = p.t.pos;
        let v = parse_value(p)?;
        let k = v.type_desc();
        match &kind {
            None => kind = Some(k),
            Some(prev) => {
                if *prev != k {
                    return Err(ParseError {
                        msg: TokErr::MixedTypes.message(),
                        line: Some(p.t.line_of(vstart)),
                        key: None,
                    });
                }
            }
        }
        out.push(v);
        skip_ws_comments_newlines(p)?;
        match p.peek()? {
            Some((Token::Comma, _, _)) => {
                p.next()?;
            }
            Some((Token::RightBracket, _, _)) => {
                p.next()?;
                break;
            }
            None => return Err(eof_err(p)),
            Some((t, a, _)) => return Err(want_err(p, a, "a comma", token_name(&t))),
        }
    }
    Ok(Value::Array(out))
}
</output>

def cmp_files(name, files, runs, envf=None, args_pre=None):
    import subprocess, os
    outs=[]
    for prog in ("/tmp/mine/executable","/workspace/executable"):
        base="/tmp/t5_"+os.path.basename(prog)+"_"+name
        shutil.rmtree(base, ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(base)
        for fn, content in files.items():
            open(os.path.join(base,fn),'w').write(content)
        o=[]
        for r in (args_pre or []):
            rr=subprocess.run([prog]+r,cwd=base,capture_output=True,text=True)
            o.append(("PRE "+" ".join(r),rr.returncode,rr.stdout,rr.stderr))
        for a in runs:
            rr=subprocess.run([prog]+a,cwd=base,capture_output=True,text=True)
            o.append((" ".join(a),rr.returncode,rr.stdout,rr.stderr))
        cfg=None
        for fn in ("c.toml","pier.toml"):
            p=os.path.join(base,fn)
            if os.path.exists(p): cfg=(fn, open(p,'rb').read())
        o.append(("FILE",cfg))
        outs.append(o)
    ok=True
    for a,b in zip(outs[0],outs[1]):
        if a!=b:
            ok=False; print("### DIFF %s %r\n   mine=%r\n   orig=%r" % (name,a[0],a[1:],b[1:]))
    return ok

fn run() -> i32 {
    let bin = bin_name();
    let argv: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    let root = cli::build_root();
    let outcome = match clap::parse(&root, &argv, &bin, true, &bin) {
        Ok(o) => o,
        Err(e) => return handle_clap(e),
    };
    let mut m = outcome.matches;
    let verbose = m.is_present("verbose");
    let explicit = m.value_of("config-file").map(PathBuf::from);
    let (sub, sub_args) = match outcome.sub {
        Some(s) => s,
        None => {
            if let Err(e) = clap::validate(&root, &mut m, &bin, &bin) {
                return handle_clap(e);
            }
            return run_alias(&m, explicit.as_ref(), verbose);
        }
    };
    let sub_static: &'static str = if sub == "help" {
        "help"
    } else {
        match clap::find_sub(&root, &sub) {
            Some(sd) => sd.name,
            None => return fail("unknown subcommand"),
        }
    };
    let cmd = if sub_static == "help" {
        cli::build_help_sub()
    } else {
        match cli::build_sub(sub_static) {
            Some(c) => c,
            None => return fail("unknown subcommand"),
        }
    };
    let prefix = format!("{} {}", bin, sub_static);
    let out = match clap::parse(&cmd, &sub_args, &prefix, false, &bin) {
        Ok(o) => o,
        Err(e) => return handle_clap(e),
    };
    let mut sm = out.matches;
    if let Err(e) = clap::validate(&cmd, &mut sm, &prefix, &bin) {
        return handle_clap(e);
    }
    match sub.as_str() {
        "add" => cmd_add(&sm, explicit.as_ref()),
        "config-init" => cmd_config_init(&sm, explicit.as_ref()),
        "copy" => cmd_copy(&sm, explicit.as_ref()),
        "edit" => cmd_edit(&sm, explicit.as_ref()),
        "list" => cmd_list(&sm, explicit.as_ref()),
        "move" => cmd_move(&sm, explicit.as_ref()),
        "remove" => cmd_remove(&sm, explicit.as_ref()),
        "run" => cmd_run(&sm, explicit.as_ref(), verbose),
        "show" => cmd_show(&sm, explicit.as_ref()),
        "help" => cmd_help(&sm, &bin),
        _ => fail("unknown subcommand"),
    }
}

fn resolve(explicit: Option<&PathBuf>) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    match config::resolve(explicit) {
        config::Resolved::Path(p) => Ok(p),
        config::Resolved::NotFound => {
            Err("No default config file found. See help for more info.".to_string())
        }
    }
}

#!/bin/bash
# Build the `pier` executable from source.
#
# The crate has no external dependencies, so a plain offline build works
# everywhere as long as a Rust toolchain (cargo/rustc) is available.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

if ! command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    for d in "${CARGO_HOME:-/usr/local/cargo}/bin" "$HOME/.cargo/bin" /usr/local/cargo/bin; do
        if [ -x "$d/cargo" ]; then
            export PATH="$d:$PATH"
            break
        fi
    done
fi

cargo build --release --offline

cp -f target/release/pier ./executable
chmod +x ./executable
EOF
chmod +x compile.sh && ./compile.sh 2>&1|tail -2 && ls -la executable && ./executable --version && git add -A && git commit -q -m "Harden compile.sh cargo lookup" && git log --oneline | head -2

## Approach

I reverse-engineered `pier 0.1.6` (a script catalog/runner by Benjamin Scholtz) **entirely by black-box observation** â running the binary with different flags, env vars, and config files, and comparing outputs byte-for-byte.

## Key discoveries (all from observation)

| Area | Finding |
|---|---|
| CLI framework | clap 2.x: bin_name from `argv[0]`'s file name, version from the app name (`pier 0.1.6`), `-h` short vs `--help` long help, term width **120** when not a TTY |
| Error text | exact formats incl. `"AliasAlreadyExists:  <alias>"` (double space), `"Unable to read config from file X: â¦ (os error 2) "` (trailing space), green ANSI hints in "Did you mean â¦" (hardcoded, independent of the colorizer) |
| Suggestions | strsim's `jaro_winkler` with threshold `> 0.8` over subcommand names **and** aliases |
| Config path chain | `-c` / `$PIER_CONFIG_PATH` used literally â `./pier.toml` â `config_dir()/pier/config.toml` â `â¦/config` â `â¦/pier.toml` â `$HOME/.pier.toml` â `$HOME/.pier` |
| `config-init` | only `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`dirs::config_dir()` (no HOME fallback logic), single-level `create_dir`, seeds a `hello-pier` example, prints **before** writing |
| TOML | `toml` 0.5.x with `to_string_pretty`: literal `'â¦'` â multiline `'''â¦'''` â basic `"â¦"`; arrays inline when `len<=1`; plus all its parse/deser error strings |
| Table | `≖` borders / `⋮` separators, columns padded by **unicode display width** (EAW-derived tables, built empirically) |
| run | `/bin/sh -c <command> <alias> <argsâ¦>`; stdout piped and written raw, stderr captured, lossy-decoded and printed **with an extra newline**; stdin inherited; signal-exits â 0 |
| edit | temp file `/tmp/xvrqt_scrawl_<pid>_0`, `$EDITOR` (default `vi`), no trimming, two distinct error messages |

## Result

A **dependency-free Rust reimplementation** (7 modules, ~3.6k lines) that compiles offline with `cargo build --release --offline`. Validated by ~25 curated scenario suites plus ~3,000 fuzz cases (CLI args, TOML contents, config paths) with zero diffs against the original.
